## TL;DR  
The current heuristic

```js
if (layer.type === 'symbol' &&
    layer.layout['text-anchor'] === undefined &&
    layer.layout['symbol-placement'] === 'point') {
    // → “shield”
}
```

is **not reliable**.  
* `text‑anchor` is *often* omitted on ordinary place‑name layers (the default is `"center"`), so the test will fire on any point‑label layer that does not explicitly set an anchor.  
* `symbol‑placement: "point"` is also the default for *any* point‑symbol layer – it says nothing about shields at all.  

Consequently you end up tagging plain POI / place‑name layers as shields and missing the real shield layers that happen to set an explicit `text‑anchor` or use a more complex `symbol-placement` expression.

Below is a short‑but‑complete guide to a **more robust heuristic** that works for the standard OSM‑Bright / OSM‑Liberty shield implementations (and for most custom shields that follow the same pattern).

---

## 1. What a “route‑shield” layer *actually looks like* in a style

| Property | Typical value / pattern | Why it matters |
|----------|------------------------|----------------|
| `type` | `"symbol"` | Shields are drawn as symbols (icon + text). |
| `layout['icon-image']` | **Expression** that resolves to a sprite name, e.g. `"{network}_{ref_length}"` or `"road_{ref_length}"` (or a literal like `"us-interstate_2"`). | The badge behind the number is always an **icon** taken from the sprite sheet. |
| `layout['text-field']` | **Expression** that resolves to the route number, e.g. `"{ref}"` (or `"I {ref}"`). | The *number* itself is rendered as text, not part of the sprite. |
| `layout['icon-text-fit']` | `"both"` / `"width"` (optional) **or** omitted (most OSM‑Bright shields use pre‑drawn badges, so `icon-text-fit` is *absent*). | If present, it tells you the badge is *stretchable* – a clear shield‑specific flag. |
| `layout['symbol-placement']` | `"point"` **or** a **zoom‑function** that switches between `"point"` and `"line"` (e.g. `{ "base": 1, "stops": [[7,"point"],[8,"line"]] }`). | Shields are placed on the *line* of a road at higher zooms, but they still have a point fallback. |
| `layout['text-font']` | Usually an array like `["Open Sans Bold","Arial Unicode MS Regular"]`. | Not unique, but most shield layers set a font explicitly. |
| `layout['text-size']` | Often a function of zoom (e.g. `["interpolate",["linear"],["zoom"],5,12,10,16]`). | Again not unique, but helps to separate “label‑only” layers that use a constant size. |
| `layout['icon-allow-overlap']` / `icon-overlap` | Often `true` or `"always"` (shields need to stay visible). | Not a must‑have, but many shield layers turn overlap on. |
| `paint['icon-color']` / `icon-halo-*` | **Absent** (shields are *not* SDF). | If you see `sdf: true` or halo settings, you’re probably looking at a generic POI icon, not a shield. |

**Key take‑away:**  
A shield layer **always** has an **`icon-image`** that is *derived* from the feature properties (`network`, `ref_length`, etc.) **and** a **`text-field`** that is derived from the feature’s `ref`. Plain place‑name layers have **no `icon-image`** (or they use a static POI icon that does *not* contain placeholders).

---

## 2. Why the old heuristic fails

| Heuristic condition | What it actually matches | Why it’s a false‑positive |
|---------------------|--------------------------|---------------------------|
| `layout['text-anchor'] === undefined` | *Any* symbol layer that does not explicitly set an anchor (the default is `"center"`). | Most POI / place‑name layers omit this property. |
| `layout['symbol-placement'] === 'point'` | *Any* point‑symbol layer that does not use a zoom‑function or line placement. | Shields also use `"point"` at low zooms, but many other layers do too. |
| **Combined** | *All* point‑symbol layers that rely on defaults → a huge superset of shields. | Hence you tag everything that looks like a simple point label. |

In short: **the two conditions are *necessary* for shields but *far from sufficient*.** They do not discriminate between “icon‑plus‑text” (shield) and “text‑only” (place name).

---

## 3. A better heuristic – step‑by‑step

Below is a **minimal** yet reliable set of checks that you can implement in a style‑audit script. Feel free to add extra “nice‑to‑have” checks (e.g. `icon-allow-overlap`) if you want stricter filtering.

```js
/**
 * Returns true if a symbol layer looks like a route‑shield layer.
 *
 * @param {object} layer – a layer object from a MapLibre style
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
function isShieldLayer(layer) {
  // 1️⃣ Must be a symbol layer
  if (layer.type !== 'symbol') return false;

  const layout = layer.layout || {};

  // 2️⃣ Must have BOTH an icon and a text field
  if (!layout['icon-image'] || !layout['text-field']) return false;

  // 3️⃣ The icon-image must be *dynamic* (contains a placeholder)
  //    – most OSM styles use "{network}_{ref_length}" or similar.
  const iconImg = layout['icon-image'];
  const isDynamicIcon =
    typeof iconImg === 'string' && /\{.*\}/.test(iconImg) || // string expression with placeholders
    Array.isArray(iconImg) && iconImg.some(v => typeof v === 'string' && /\{.*\}/.test(v)); // expression array

  if (!isDynamicIcon) return false;

  // 4️⃣ The text-field must be dynamic and reference the route number
  const txt = layout['text-field'];
  const isDynamicText =
    typeof txt === 'string' && /\{ref/.test(txt) || // e.g. "{ref}" or "I {ref}"
    Array.isArray(txt) && txt.some(v => typeof v === 'string' && /\{ref/.test(v));

  if (!isDynamicText) return false;

  // 5️⃣ (Optional but useful) – shields are *not* SDF icons
  //    If the style explicitly marks the icon as SDF, it’s probably a POI.
  if (layout['icon-sdf'] === true) return false; // rarely set, but safe

  // 6️⃣ (Optional) – check for stretchable badges
  //    If icon-text-fit is set to anything other than "none", we are definitely dealing with a shield.
  const fit = layout['icon-text-fit'];
  if (fit && fit !== 'none') return true; // stretchable badge → shield

  // 7️⃣ (Optional) – check that the icon name contains a ref‑length suffix
  //    This catches the pre‑drawn badge style (e.g. "us-interstate_2").
  if (typeof iconImg === 'string' && /_\d+$/.test(iconImg)) return true;

  // 8️⃣ If we got here, we have a dynamic icon + dynamic text → treat as shield.
  return true;
}
```

### Why this works

| Check | What it filters out | What it keeps |
|-------|---------------------|---------------|
| **`icon-image` present** | Pure text‑only place‑name layers | Anything that draws a badge (including shields) |
| **`text-field` present** | POI icons that have no label (e.g. “cafe” icons) | Layers that render a number/label on top of the badge |
| **Dynamic placeholder in `icon-image`** | Static POI icons like `"cafe"` or `"park"` | Shields that use `{network}_{ref_length}` or `"road_{ref_length}"` |
| **Dynamic placeholder in `text-field`** | Layers that label a feature with a name (`{name}`) | Shields that show the route reference (`{ref}`) |
| **Exclude `icon-sdf:true`** | SDF icons (colored POIs) | Shields (which are *not* SDF) |
| **`icon-text-fit` not `"none"`** | Pre‑drawn badge shields (optional) – *if present* it’s a *definite* shield. |
| **`/_\d+$/` suffix** | Catches the pre‑drawn badge variant (`us-interstate_2`, `road_3`, …) even if the placeholder was already resolved by the server. |

You can drop the optional steps (6‑8) if you want a *looser* detection, but the core three checks (`icon-image` + `text-field` + placeholders) already separate **most** shields from ordinary place‑name layers.

---

## 4. Real‑world examples

| Layer (OSM‑Bright) | `icon-image` | `text-field` | Heuristic result |
|--------------------|--------------|--------------|------------------|
| `highway-shield-us-interstate` | `"{network}_{ref_length}"` | `"{ref}"` | **Shield** (passes all checks) |
| `highway-shield-us-highway` | `"{network}_{ref_length}"` | `"{ref}"` | **Shield** |
| `place-label-city` | *absent* | `"{name}"` | **Not a shield** (fails #2) |
| `poi-label-cafe` | `"cafe"` | `"{name}"` | **Not a shield** (fails dynamic placeholder) |
| `road-label` (generic line label) | *absent* | `"{name}"` | **Not a shield** |
| Custom “stretchable” shield | `"road"` (with `stretchX/Y` & `content`) | `"{ref}"` | **Shield** (passes #2, #3, #4; optional #6 catches it) |

---

## 5. Edge cases & how to handle them

| Situation | Why the basic heuristic might miss it | Fix |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|-----|
| **Shield layer that uses a *static* icon name** (e.g. `"us-interstate_2"` pre‑rendered for a specific ref length) | No placeholder → step 3 fails. | Keep the optional suffix check (`/_\d+$/`) – most static badge names end with `_1…_6`. |
| **Shield layer that deliberately sets `icon-sdf: true`** (rare, only if you want a color‑tintable badge) | Step 5 would reject it. | Remove the `icon-sdf` exclusion or make it configurable. |
| **Place‑name layer that also uses an icon** (e.g. a city dot with a small circle icon) | It has `icon-image` but the icon is static (`"circle-11"`). | The placeholder test (`/\{.*\}/`) will filter it out because the icon name is literal. |
| **Custom shield that uses a *different* placeholder name** (e.g. `{shield}` instead of `{network}`) | Regex `/\{ref/` may miss it. | Generalise the text‑field check to any placeholder that contains `ref` or `ref_` – e.g. `/\{.*ref.*\}/i`. |
| **Shield layer that uses a *function* expression** (e.g. `["case", ["==", ["get","network"], "us-interstate"], "us-interstate_2", "road_1"]`) | The placeholder test on a string fails because the value is an array. | The helper `isDynamicIcon` above already walks an expression array and looks for any string containing `{…}` *or* a numeric suffix.
